title: P-256 sigma rho: concentrated two-cycle cost and residual Markov reserve

claims.statement: For uniform full-size P-256 targets Q=[x]P, the classical cold algorithm specified in proof.md and the included predecessor specification recovers x with probability at least 0.39 under the explicitly retained H1, M1/L-ori/global fresh-class exposure and H3 premises. All preprocessing, failures, restarts, memory transfers, lookup, replay, verification and output are charged. The total computation is at most 2^127.241865 target-group-operation equivalents at C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions per unit. The change separates fresh-source two-cycle entries with an adapted Chernoff bound from residual rare work with a factor-849 Markov reserve. The common batched path is charged by its anchor schedule: the measured plain round at every step and the measured anchor-round excess only in the batch rounds divisible by 64, a deterministic count. It uses tau=496471/1000000 and eta=2^-16 with the unchanged 2^16 adders, 2^32 walks and distinguished-point probability 2^-60. Peak memory is at most 2^77 bytes, preprocessing is at most 2^50 units and is included, and nonuniform advice is zero bytes. The probability calculation is conditional on the disclosed heuristics and the arithmetic pricing on H3; these are not certified at production trajectory lengths. Historical evidence is attributed and its measured scope retained.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the revised full production cost ledger and order certificate, then run the inherited complete reduced-order procedure at tau=0.4965, retaining failures and replay checks. The two results have distinct scopes; neither establishes production mixing.
